newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Nikkei futures surge at end, more gains seen.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Nikkei futures surge at end, more gains seen.

text.p: SIMEX Nikkei futures shot to a buoyant finish on Tuesday on stop-loss buying as the underlying cash market took its cue from the Dow's record close above 6,000 points overnight.
Dealers said the benchmark Nikkei 225 December contract looked set for further gains but was likely to encounter resistance near its last high of 21,670, seen in late September.
The contract finished 10 points off an intra-day high of 21,505 against a previous settlement at 21,140. Volume remained relatively low at 14,000 lots.
Stop-loss buy orders were triggered above 21,350, taking the December Nikkei quickly to 21,505.
"People had been trying to short the Nikkei but it was refusing to go down with (Japanese) bonds coming under pressure and dollar/yen staying firm," said a trader at a European house.
But he said the December Nikkei would have difficulty appreciating above 21,670-21,700 ahead of Japan's October 20 general election, unless the dollar reached 113 yen.
A chartist with a local institution said the December Nikkei's close above 21,460 boded well for further gains.
"Even with this move, the 21,355 level has to be supported to maintain the uptrend," he added.
